source: Müller et al. (2019) plate motion model v2.0 (Tectonics, doi:10.1029/2018TC005462), 250-0 Ma, and Young et al. (2019) (Geoscience Frontiers, doi:10.1016/j.gsf.2018.05.011) 410-250 Ma rotations, as distributed in GPlates/pygplates-tutorials (EarthByte Group)
rights: CC BY 3.0 Unported, EarthByte Group (pygplates-tutorials LICENSE.md). Credit the EarthByte Group and cite Müller et al. 2019.
format: polys: [plate index, from_age, to_age, lat0, lon0, dlat, dlon, ...] in 0.01 degrees, present-day positions; quats: per plate, [w, x, y, z] at each of ages
limits: Coastlines simplified to about 0.2 degrees; outer rings only. Continents only, no plate boundaries or ocean floor. The 410-250 Ma rotations are older and less certain than the 250-0 Ma part. Longitude before ~200 Ma is weakly constrained in any model.
